name: Mituo Village
technique: Buddha-recitation (nianfo) practice periods combining chanting, walking, and sitting cultivation, following the teachings of Master Chin Kung
influences: Pure Land sutras (Amitabha Sutra, Infinite Life Sutra, Contemplation Sutra)
teacherAccess: Resident Buddhist Venerables lead group practice sessions and give dharma talks throughout each retreat; informal access to teachers is available on-site.
retreatOptions: Quarterly multi-day residential retreats, typically running about 5-7 days, in addition to biweekly weekend group-practice sessions.
schedule: Retreat days follow a monastic-style timetable of six or more chanting/recitation periods from roughly 4:30am wake-up to 9pm lights-out, with breakfast and lunch served between sessions.
cost: Free / donation-based - Mituo Village never charges a fee for retreats, meals, or lodging, though donations are welcomed.

pricePerDay.notes: Strictly donation-based: the center explicitly does not charge for attending retreats, including meals and boarding, and sets no suggested amount.

foodNotes: Communal vegetarian meals (breakfast and lunch) are provided free of charge during retreats, in keeping with Pure Land Buddhist practice.
workNotes: No work practice is required of retreat participants; the resident nuns maintain the property and are supported by donations.
about: Mituo Village is the retreat property of the Amitabha Buddhist Society of Philadelphia, a Pure Land Buddhist community following the teachings of the late Master Chin Kung. Purchased in 2014 from a United Church of Christ conference that had run it as a summer camp (Camp Mensch Mill) since 1928, the 140-acre site in Alburtis, Pennsylvania includes dormitories, a main hall, and a large statue of Amitabha Buddha. Resident Venerables lead quarterly multi-day retreats of roughly five to seven days built around communal Buddha-recitation (nianfo) practice periods, chanting, and dharma talks, along with more frequent biweekly weekend group-practice sessions. True to Pure Land teaching on generosity, Mituo Village never charges for retreats, meals, or lodging, relying entirely on voluntary donations from a mostly Chinese and Vietnamese diaspora sangha that travels from across the East Coast.
